# Wix CLI Commands

The CLI's commands are described in three places, kept in sync so that each reflects the whole
command surface: `wix --help` (from the command definitions in this repository), this file
(shipped with `@wix/cli`, read by agents working in a project), and the reference at
https://dev.wix.com/docs/wix-cli/command-reference (source: `wix-private/developer-docs`,
`cli-portal/reference/`). A command added, removed or changed lands in all three.

Which commands exist depends on where you run `wix`: outside any project only the account
commands are available; inside a folder with a `wix.config.json` (or `wix.config.mjs`) the project commands appear as
well; a few apply only to app projects. Creating a project is a separate package, invoked through
`npm create`, and is what you run before a `wix.config.json` (or `wix.config.mjs`) exists. Hidden and deprecated flags are
not listed here or in `--help`.

## Before a project exists: create one

Run these in the parent folder (they create the project folder) or, for `link` and `init`, in the
existing project's root. They sign you in if needed.

### `npm create @wix/new@latest app`

Create a new Wix app project: registers a new app in your account (or extends an existing one)
and scaffolds from a template.

**Options:**

- `--app-name <app-name>`: The name for your new app.
- `-t, --template <template-id>`: Template ID to use for the app creation.
- `--extend-app-id <extend-app-id>`: The ID of the app you want to extend (conflicts with `--template`).

### `npm create @wix/new@latest headless`

Create a new Wix headless site: provisions a Wix business and site, scaffolds from a template,
initializes local files.

**Options:**

- `--business-name <business-name>`: The name of your business (required for a non-interactive run).
- `--folder-name <folder-name>`: The name of your project folder.
- `--site-template [site-template]`: Site template to use for the app creation.
- `--skip-install`: Skip automatic dependency installation.
- `--skip-git`: Skip initializing a Git repository during setup.
- `--no-publish`: Do not publish your site at the end of the creation.

### `npm create @wix/new@latest headless link`

Link the current project (an Astro 5 project without `wix.config.json`) to Wix as its deployment
target: provisions a business and site, writes `wix.config.json` and `.env.local`.

**Options:**

- `--business-name <business-name>`: The name of your business (required for a non-interactive run).

### `npm create @wix/new@latest init`

Initialize a Wix headless project in the current folder in one step, without prompts: signs you
in, creates the project (named after the folder, from the blank template) and writes the generated
configuration into the current folder as `wix.config.json`. It creates no new folder and changes
no other file; run it in a folder that has no `wix.config.json` yet.

## Anywhere: account commands

Available with or without a project.

### `wix login`

Log in to your Wix account

**Options:**

- `--api-key <token>`: Authenticate using an API key for automations and CI environments

### `wix logout`

Log out of your Wix account

### `wix whoami`

Display the email of the logged in Wix user

### `wix token`

Print the current access token, refreshing if needed. Use it inline for direct REST API calls:
`-H "Authorization: $(wix token --site <site-id>)"`; tokens are short-lived, mint one per command.

**Options:**

- `-s, --site <site-id>`: Get a site-scoped access token

### `wix telemetry <on|off>`

Opt in/out of sending anonymous usage information (telemetry) to Wix

### `wix account`

Manage your Wix account

**Options:**

- `--site-id <siteId>`: Site ID to scope account commands to a specific site

**Subcommands:**

- `wix account domain suggest <query>`: Suggest available domains based on a keyword, brand, or business idea
  - `-l, --limit <number>`: Number of suggestions to return (1-20)
  - `-t, --tld <tld...>`: Filter by up to 10 TLDs, without the dot (for example, com net)
  - `--json`: Output in JSON format
- `wix account domain checkout-link <domain>`: Get a checkout link to buy a domain for your Wix account. No charge is made until the purchase is completed in the browser.
  - `--json`: Output in JSON format

## Inside a project: project commands

Available in a folder with a `wix.config.json` or `wix.config.mjs` (a headless site or an app project created by the
Wix CLI). Run them from the project root.

### `wix dev`

Start the local development server.

**Options:**

- `--port <port>`: Specify which port to run on. Defaults to 4321.
- `--allowed-hosts <allowedHosts>`: Specify a comma-separated list of allowed hosts or allow any hostname.

For app projects in non-interactive environments, select or create a development site with `wix dev-site` before running `wix dev`.

### `wix build`

Invoke the astro build process, forwarding all command-line arguments.

### `wix preview`

Create a preview deployment of your application. It takes no options.

### `wix release`

Release a new version of your application.

**Options:**

- `-c, --comment <comment>`: The comment for your release version, not visible by users
- `-t, --version-type <type>`: The type of version you would like to create (major or minor)

### `wix generate`

Generate a new extension for your project.

**Options:**

- `--type <type>`: Extension type to generate (conflicts with `--params`). Available types:
  - `DASHBOARD_PAGE`: A page in the Wix dashboard
  - `DASHBOARD_MODAL`: A modal dialog in the Wix dashboard
  - `DASHBOARD_PLUGIN`: A plugin for the Wix dashboard
  - `DASHBOARD_MENU_PLUGIN`: A menu plugin for the Wix dashboard
  - `EMBEDDED_SCRIPT`: An embedded script extension
  - `CUSTOM_ELEMENT`: A custom HTML element
  - `SITE_PLUGIN`: A plugin for Wix sites
  - `EVENT`: An event handler
  - `SERVICE_PLUGIN`: A service plugin (SPI implementation)
- `--params <json>`: Generate an extension non-interactively from a JSON object (conflicts with `--type`); `wix schema generate` prints the shape it expects.

### `wix schema`

Print machine-readable schemas for CLI commands.

**Subcommands:**

- `wix schema generate`: Print a JSON schema of all available extension types and their required inputs
  - `--type <type>`: Print the schema for a single extension type instead of the full schema

### `wix skills`

Manage Wix skills in your project.

**Subcommands:**

- `wix skills add`: Add Wix skills to your project
- `wix skills update`: Update installed skills to the latest version

### `wix env`

Work with environment variables.

**Subcommands:**

#### `wix env pull`

Pulls environment variables and merge them into .env.local file.

#### `wix env set`

Sets an environment variable.

**Options:**

- `--key <key>`: Name of the variable (required)
- `--value <value>`: Value of the variable (required)

#### `wix env remove`

Removes an environment variable.

**Options:**

- `--key <key>`: Name of the variable (required)

## Inside an app project only

Available when `wix.config.json` has `"projectType": "App"`.

### `wix dev-site`

Manage the development site used by the current app.

**Subcommands:**

- `wix dev-site list [--search <query>]`: List account sites. Search matches site names, display names, and domains.
- `wix dev-site current`: Show the effective site ID and whether it came from `WIX_SITE_ID` or app config.
- `wix dev-site select <site-id>`: Validate and select a site, waiting for app installation when required.
- `wix dev-site create [--template dev|harmony] [--select]`: Create a development site and optionally select it.

`WIX_SITE_ID` takes precedence over the site saved in app config.

## Other project kinds

Projects created with the earlier app framework (`@wix/cli-app`) and Wix Code site projects
have their own command sets, not listed here; `wix --help` inside such a project shows them.
